segment.source: Questions that **fold open** to their answers.
External advisors with their **affiliation and subject**.
Former members with **their years and where they went**.
In-page section links in a **bar that sticks** while scrolling.
**Title, standfirst, byline and lead image** at the top of an article.
A quiet **byline strip**: date, reading time, category, author.
A compact **byline block** under an article.
Award emblems in a row with **prize and year**.
A slim band: **back arrow and the parent page's title**.
Each measure **twice: from, to, and the change**.
The **trail from the root** to the current page.
A **bordered note** that steps out of the reading flow.
One project's results as a **row of figures**.
One project: **mark, problem, headline result, link**.
A taxonomy as a **wrapping row of pills**, current one marked.
Compliance **seals with their scope** and a register link.
The **numbered chapters** of a long work, across pages.
Customer names as **plain text columns**, no logos needed.
**Code in a monospaced panel** with language and file name.
Figures about the **people around a product**.
One named contact: **portrait, role, how to reach them**.
A **boxed table of contents** for the page it sits on.
Many **small avatars with names**, densely tiled.
**Store badges beside a device shot**, with platform requirements.
**We call you back** — hours, waiting time, and the request button.
The **band that ends a page** — one heading, one button, one quiet link.
**Where to join in** — forum, chat, user group, each with its size.
The **frame around a contact form** — copy, promise, button.
**Every route to you** — chat, phone, email, help centre, with hours.
**One person as the way in** — portrait, a sentence, two ways to reach them.
**One slim row** — icon, a line, a button. Drops into running text.
A CTA with a **row of trust marks** directly beneath it.
A CTA in **two halves** — copy and buttons beside an image.
A **sticky bottom bar** — pure CSS, alive only within its section.
**Time or scarcity** as the argument — a stated deadline, never a countdown.
**Book a live demo** — length, host, agenda, calendar button.
**Date, place, price** as a spec, with the registration button.
**What the long form asks** — steps, time, what to have ready.
A **real excerpt, then the ask** — a visual gate, not an access check.
**A file for an address** — cover, three takeaways, one button.
**Subscribe to the letter** — copy and button; the form lives elsewhere.
A **closable offer** — full-width bar or corner card, remembers the close.
**Become a partner** — what you get, what is expected, how to apply.
**Two or three ways to buy** — self-serve, sales, partner.
**Invite, they join, both gain** — three steps and the reward.
**Answer a questionnaire** — topic, minutes, what happens with it.
**Start the trial** — the ask, with the objections answered beside it.
**Join the queue** — what is coming, roughly when, how many wait.
**Workplace photos** beside a paragraph on how you work.
An **excerpt from a case study**, with the mark and a read-on link.
**Where a total goes**: share bar plus the amount, line by line.
**One bar per item**, lengths from the typed percentages.
**Two bars per criterion**: your figure against a reference figure.
**One figure** at display size with unit, caption and optional action.
Criteria rows with a **tick** and the alternative's answer beside it.
**Three to six bare numbers** across a tinted band, one word each.
How one total **splits across buckets**, one bar per bucket.
**One target**: percentage reached, the figures in words, a deadline.
**Text on one side, figures on the other** — numbers with an argument.
**Two to four** metric cards: figure, label, one line of context.
A **numbered ranking** with the figure at the end of each row.
**Where the figures come from**: period, sample, method, source.
A **compact label-left, figure-right list** for narrow columns.
One figure plus its **change** against a named earlier period.
**One to four rings**, each filled to its typed percentage.
Named rows, each with a **bar filled** to its typed percentage.
**Ordered milestones** with a state icon and their own percentage.
An **overall score** plus per-criterion ratings as filled segments.
**One bar, several segments** — a whole read as its parts.
**Label and value pairs** — technical data, dimensions, conditions.
A **figure beside a paragraph** that explains what it means.
Services with a **state word and a coloured dot** per row.
A real **table** with a caption above and a source note below.
A **sparkline-style column strip**, one column per period.
**One tick per period**, filled to its typed availability figure.
**Term and description** pairs, one per row.
Entries **grouped by first letter**, with a letter bar on top.
**Files to take away**, with type and size.
A statement whose weight comes from **who is saying it**.
**Two states of one subject**, side by side or wiped on hover.
Tiles of **deliberately unequal size**, the first one leading.
One image with a **numbered legend** keyed to marks in the artwork.
Dense **ticked or crossed** lines in two columns, with qualifiers.
Prose on one side, a **syntax-highlighted snippet** on the other.
A capability with a **poster frame** and a play control in an overlay.
Rows that **open on click**, built on native disclosure markup.
The default **icon, title, sentence** grid in two to four columns.
A dense **multi-column index** of linked one-line capabilities.
A grid of the **tools this connects to**, each optionally linked.
Full-width rows with room for **a real paragraph** per entry.
Measured results paired with **the capability that produced them**.
Where the product runs, as **icon-led entries that link out**.
A capability beside the **customer sentence that proves it**.
One **horizontally scrolling row** with snap points, no wrapping.
A tight **icon row with one-word labels**, no descriptions.
Capabilities with a **shipped, in-progress or planned** state each.
**One capability per band**: media beside prose, points and an action.
**Name-and-value pairs** in a clean two-column table.
A **numbered sequence** along a connector: figure, title, sentence.
Intro column that **stays put** while the entry list scrolls past.
**One panel at a time** behind a row of tab buttons.
Cards that name **an audience or a job** and link to its page.
**Old way against your way**, one aligned row per point.
Stages **chained with arrows** from input through middle to output.
**Conformance level, one sentence** and links to statement and feedback.
**One location**: address, a still map image, directions link.
**Store badges** as links, optionally beside a QR image.
A thin band with **one anchor link** back to the top of the page.
**Brand statement** on one side, a **newsletter prompt** on the other.
**Seals and standards** you hold, each linked to its certificate.
**Phone, mail, address** as a list, one icon per channel.
A **named person** with portrait, role and two ways to reach them.
**One quiet line**: the copyright notice and at most two links.
**Picture credits and licences** as pairs, optionally two columns.
**Funder logos** with the sentence their conditions require.
**One number, large**, with when it is staffed and a second channel.
**Operator details** as pairs, with a link to the full imprint.
**Which version this is**, with plain links to the others.
**Imprint, privacy, terms** as one separated line of links.
Links in **two to four columns**, headings from unlinked entries.
A **one-line subscribe prompt** with a button on a tinted band.
**Several locations**: city, address lines, directions link.
**Day and time pairs**, closed days struck out, holidays as a note.
**Last reviewed, version, responsible** — the page's housekeeping line.
**Payment and delivery marks** in a row, each optionally linked.
A closing **question with one or two actions** beneath it.
The site's sections and pages as **two-level link columns**.
**Icon links to profiles**, with or without network names.
**Brand column, link columns and a quiet line** as one closing block.
**Numbered notes and sources** at the foot of an article.
The **origin narrative**, a portrait and the founder's name.
A **notice strip** fused to the top of an otherwise ordinary hero.
App opening with a **device shot** and a row of store links.
Article head with **byline, standfirst** and cover image.
One photograph **full bleed**, headline set on a scrim over it.
Short intro band above a listing, with breadcrumb and **count badge**.
Opening claim plus **three or four ticked** one-line benefits.
Claim beside a **copyable install line** or short snippet.
Docs opening with a **search field, version badge** and quick links.
Event opening with **date, venue and price** as facts, plus registration.
Opening band with a quiet **row of customer marks** beneath it.
Opening band closing on **two to four figures** with their labels.
The **smallest** opening: breadcrumb, title, one line, one action.
Welcome line over **two to four destination cards**, each linked.
Opening claim with the **entry price and period** next to the action.
A **centred** opening with two actions and the product shown beneath.
**Portrait, name and role** with a row of contact links.
An opening built on **one customer sentence**, with name and portrait.
Headline over one **large search field** with suggested queries.
Opening claim plus a **one-field** signup row and its small print.
Fixed copy over **cross-fading backdrops** with manual dots.
A **two-column** opening: copy on one side, one image on the other.
Headline left, **supporting paragraph right**, no media at all.
One **oversized claim**, no media, at most one quiet link.
**State dot** and one measured value, with a link to the history.
A **poster frame** with a play control that opens the film in an overlay.
One **picture with its caption** and credit line.
Several pictures in an **even grid** of thumbnails.
A short **inline run of links** to points further down.
A boxed list of the **points to take away**.
The **standfirst**: one or two large sentences that open a piece.
A **signed message** to the reader, with name and role.
A **few people, larger**, with a line of biography each.
Many **bare links in a dense grid**, no descriptions.
Customer **marks in an even grid**, optically sized alike.
A **wall of marks** with a claim set into the grid.
Mentors with **their subjects and a way to book them**.
Destinations as a **grid of cards** with an icon and a line each.
**One large entry** with a picture, the rest as a list beside it.
Destinations as **full-width rows** with a line of context.
**Explanation on one side, links on the other**, swappable.
Destinations in a **row that scrolls sideways**.
Each location with **its address and its contact**.
Vacancies as rows: **title, location, link to the posting**.
A **vertical contents rail** beside the text that sticks.
A **numbered pager** for a series, current part marked.
Partner marks as **linked cards**, one per partner.
**Question and answer pairs** with one named person.
One person in full: **portrait, role, biography, links**.
A colleague's card built around **something they said**.
Coverage rows: **headline, publication, link**.
Two facing links: **back to the last, on to the next**.
**Paid extras** on top of a plan — as rows or as a card grid.
**Monthly and yearly** side by side — a saving stated, not a switch.
A **bundle and its saving** — package price against the sum of parts.
A **static calculation sheet** — the inputs and the formula, no total.
A **feature-by-feature table** — as a full band or as one plan column.
**Who pays less and why** — nonprofit, education, startup rates.
The **tier with no number** — what large buyers get, and a conversation.
**Money questions** answered — accordion or open list.
**One promise**, an icon and up to four supporting points.
**Ticks and crosses** for one price — what is in it, what is not.
**Named licence editions** with their price and their scope.
**Was and now** — a struck-through price, the new one, and a deadline.
**Charges that happen once** — setup, migration, training.
The **opening band** of a pricing page — title, positioning, small print.
A **quiet row of payment marks** with one line of conditions.
**One plan** — price, feature list, button. Two to four sit side by side.
**Upgrade, downgrade, cancel** — the billing rules as questions.
**Two to four routes** to the right price list, before any number.
The **recommended tier** as its own wide band, not one card among many.
**Ask for a written price** — panel and button, form handled elsewhere.
A **volume ladder** — price per seat, band by band.
**One price, one button** — for offers that have nothing to compare.
**Cost of ownership** as figures — licence, hosting, hours, over time.
**How the trial works** — length, card, limits, and the last day.
**Price per unit**, row by row — metered rates without a total.
Arguments **for and against** in two facing columns.
A **short line lifted from the text**, set large between paragraphs.
A **slim bar of shortcuts**, icon plus two or three words.
Several quotations, **one at a time**, with arrows and dots.
A quotation **beside the face** of the person who said it.
One **aggregate score** with stars, count and source.
A few **further pages worth reading**, with context lines.
A reading list of **links that leave the site**, with sources.
Individual reviews with **stars, author and text**.
**One score per platform**, each with its own scale.
The **main prose block** — formatted body copy at a readable measure.
A **titled rule** that starts a new part of a long page.
The whole section as an **annotated index in columns**.
The **pages beside this one**, with the current one marked.
The **page tree below this page**, nested and indented.
Short **public posts** as small cards with handles.
One **keynote**: session title, abstract, speaker, slot.
Who is speaking, with **affiliation and talk title**.
**One large sentence** across the full width of the page.
Stages of a **multi-page process**, done ones marked.
Instructions as a **numbered sequence** of steps.
Passages of text as **tabs**, one panel at a time.
**One department per band**: title, description, its people.
**Overlapping portraits** with a count and one sentence.
Names in **columns headed by function**, no portraits.
Everyone at **equal size**: portrait, name, role.
One **wide group portrait** with a caption and name key.
The **words above a team grid** — no portraits of its own.
A large team as **dense, scannable rows**.
Figures about the team: **headcount, tenure, languages**.
Quotes on a **sliding track** with previous and next controls.
Several **quote cards** side by side in a grid.
A quote and the **one number** it earned, side by side.
A quote next to a **large portrait** of the person who said it.
One **customer quote**, its author, and nothing else.
A **video poster** and a pull quote that link to the recording.
Two passages of prose in **facing columns**.
**Prose and a picture** side by side, swappable left to right.
**Dated entries** down a line, in order.
Icon and **short promise** pairs, sized to sit beside a CTA.
**One wide card** pointing at the single next thing.
**One big count** with a short row of marks beneath.
A **video in a 16:9 frame** with poster image and caption.
